key_insight: Across 601 matched device pairs, mobile ions were found to have only a small effect on steady-state performance in efficient perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: For PSC design, optimizing recombination, ion density, and band offsets appears more important than treating mobile ions as the dominant steady-state bottleneck.
method: Paired comparison: each ion-enabled device matched to an identical ion-free control
Factorial analysis across ion density, recombination rate, band offsets, and contact architectures (n-i-p / p-i-n)
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 601 pairs of simulated perovskite solar cells over a broad physically relevant parameter space and compared ion-containing devices directly against ion-free counterparts.
watch_item: Results are based on steady-state modeling, so transient behaviors, degradation, and device-to-device fabrication variability may still change the practical impact of mobile ions.
paper_title: An Investigation into the Effect of Mobile Ions on the Steady State Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
